sections.h2: What is Columbiana County like for a house owner, and who sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
Columbiana County sits on the eastern edge of Ohio, with Pennsylvania on its east line, the Ohio River and Jefferson and Carroll counties to the south, Carroll and Stark counties to the west and Mahoning County to the north. It covers about 534 square miles in eighteen townships. Lisbon is the county seat and Salem is the largest city, and the county forms part of Appalachian Ohio.

The county auditor, at 105 S. Market Street in Lisbon, sets values and takes deeds for transfer; the number is 330-424-9515. The treasurer collects the tax and answers at 330-424-9514. Cash payments are taken at the counter between eight and four on weekdays. The recorder, at 330-424-9517, files the deed after the auditor has processed it.

East Liverpool was home to what the county's own account and Wikipedia describe as the largest pottery industry in the world, and the county's river towns carry that industrial history. Salem, Wellsville, East Palestine and Columbiana are other places a seller might name on a deed.

sections.h2: What dates does the Columbiana County treasurer post for tax payments?
sections.html:
Bills go out twice a year, usually in January and July, and Ohio bills a year behind. The treasurer's home page lists tentative 2027 dates: March 5, 2027 for first-half 2026 taxes and July 30, 2027 for second-half 2026 taxes. Treat those as the dates to confirm before closing a sale in either window.

Mail that carries a postmark from the due date or earlier is treated as on time. The treasurer prints a 5% penalty for payments made within ten days after the due date and 10% after that, and delinquent accounts add interest at a rate the Ohio Tax Commissioner sets each year. The statute behind the split is section 323.121, which waives half the penalty when full payment arrives inside ten days.

  • Cash, checks, money orders and cashier's checks are taken at the counter. Do not mail cash.
  • Online payment runs through a provider that charges 2.95% on cards with a $2.00 minimum, 2.50% per transaction on ACH, and 2.95% plus $0.95 for a card payment by phone, as the treasurer prints them.
  • For a paid receipt by mail, return the whole bill with a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: How does Columbiana County value property?
sections.html:
Every six years the auditor hires a professional appraisal firm to set market value. Between those, the Ohio Department of Taxation looks at sales and economic factors every three years, and the auditor adjusts values to match. A house worth more after a reappraisal does not guarantee a higher bill, because voters decide levies and the second factor in the treasurer's explanation is the ballot box.

Columbiana County government collects almost nothing from real estate tax. The treasurer's site says the county takes only a 0.2 mill for debt retirement after the commissioners chose to waive a 2 mill levy and rely on sales tax. So a bill in Salem or Lisbon is made up mostly of school, township, city or village, library and voted special levies.

If a mortgage servicer pays the tax from escrow, tell the treasurer in writing when the loan is paid off or refinanced. The office states that a lender must notify it of changes in writing, and the office asks anyone who should have received a bill and did not to call at once.

sections.h2: What options does a Columbiana County owner have to challenge a valuation?
sections.html:
An owner who thinks a valuation is wrong can use the county Board of Revision, the Ohio Department of Taxation, or Common Pleas Court. The treasurer's FAQ points to a Board of Revision complaint filed by March 31, processed through the auditor's office at 330-424-9515. The statute, section 5715.19, can allow a later cutoff when first-half collection closes after March 31.

A late-fee complaint is a separate paper. The treasurer's office handles requests to remove a penalty; call 330-424-9514 for the form and write down why the late charge should not apply.

sections.h2: Which credits and special valuations apply in Columbiana County?
sections.html:
The treasurer's page on real estate credits describes four programs, and the auditor takes every application.

  • 10% rollback: a long-standing reduction for residential real estate not used in a business.
  • 2.5% rollback: for a homestead, meaning the dwelling plus up to one acre, with an application certifying primary residence.
  • Homestead exemption: for homeowners 65 or older and those permanently and totally disabled, for a dwelling and up to one acre. Ask the auditor for the current income limit and filing window, since both have changed over the years.
  • Current agricultural use value: land with ten acres in commercial farming, or fewer than ten acres averaging at least $2,500 of yearly gross farm income, after three years of qualifying use. When land leaves the program, a charge equal to the extra tax over the previous three years applies.

Timber land run under state forestry rules may be taxed at half the local rate. A buyer taking over farm acreage should find out whether the parcel is enrolled before agreeing on a price.

sections.h2: How many people and homes does Columbiana County have?
sections.html:
Residents numbered fewer in 2025 than in 2020, and a large share are past retirement age.

Nearly one resident in four is 65 or older, so Homestead and the 2.5% rollback matter to many owners. At a median home value of $151,600 against median gross rent of $756 the county sits at the lower end of Ohio's housing costs, which matters for any seller comparing a cash sale with a long listing.

sections.h2: What if a Columbiana County owner is behind on tax and wants to sell?
sections.html:
A delinquent owner can set up a five-pay contract at the treasurer's office. The delinquent amount is split into five equal installments over two and a half years, and current taxes must still be paid on time throughout. Missing an installment voids the contract and foreclosure continues.

Section 323.121 stops penalty and interest while a valid contract stays in effect, so a sale can close with the contract balance paid at the table. Request the parcel's payoff from the treasurer and let the title company re-verify it shortly before closing.

A deed in this county goes to the auditor on the state's DTE 100 conveyance form before it reaches the recorder. The recorder's fees follow Revised Code sections 317.32 and 317.36, which split the basic fee equally between the recording fee and the Ohio Housing Trust Fund, with an optional county preservation charge on top.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Columbiana County?
faqs.a: The county treasurer collects it, at 105 South Market Street in Lisbon, phone 330-424-9514. The auditor at 330-424-9515 values property and takes applications for credits.

faqs.q: When are Columbiana County second-half 2026 taxes due?
faqs.a: The treasurer's home page lists a tentative date of July 30, 2027, with first-half 2026 taxes tentatively due March 5, 2027. Confirm both with the office before relying on them.

faqs.q: What late fee does Columbiana County charge?
faqs.a: The treasurer prints 5% for payments made within ten days after the due date and 10% after that. Interest is added on delinquent accounts at a rate the Ohio Tax Commissioner sets.

faqs.q: Can I pay a delinquent Columbiana County bill in installments?
faqs.a: Yes. A five-pay contract divides the delinquency into five equal installments over about two and a half years. Current taxes must stay paid, and one missed installment voids the contract.

faqs.q: How do I dispute a Columbiana County property value?
faqs.a: File a complaint with the Board of Revision by March 31 through the auditor's office. Appeals can also go to the Ohio Department of Taxation or Common Pleas Court.
